//: The configuration this package tells consumers to use for a TypeScript acceptance suite, applied to our own
fixtures so the advice is exercised rather than just documented. See the 'How to lint WDIO/QA suites'
Two details matter. `types` names mocha rather than jest, because these are WDIO suites. And `include`
reaches the suite files themselves -- a tsconfig that only covers a runner script leaves them outside the
project, so the globals never arrive and every `describe` is an error.
Known limitation, verified here: `@wdio/globals/types` declares a global `expect` typed as
expect-webdriverio, which shadows chai's. So a chai-style `expect(x).to.be.true` does not type-check even
with `chai` added to `types`. Suites that assert with chai should import it -- `import { expect } from
'chai'` -- which is already what most of them do. The fixtures here deliberately use the global form to
exercise the ESLint relaxation, so `tsc` reports two errors on example.ts by design.
